name: De Moivre: chances and trigonometry/complex fusion
summary: De Moivre extended probability to approximation by analysis and linked powers of complex numbers to trigonometry.

name: Euler-Monge differential geometry of surfaces
summary: Clairaut, Euler and Monge studied curvature of curves and surfaces.

name: De Moivre: normal approximation to the binomial
summary: Stirling-type asymptotics were applied to binomial sums, yielding the normal curve.

name: Graph theory from the Konigsberg bridges
summary: A puzzle about walks across bridges is stripped to vertices and edges, and a parity condition settles it, an early instance of 'geometry of position'.

name: Analytic number theory I: Euler's product and Dirichlet characters
summary: Infinite series and characters of finite abelian groups (a Fourier analysis on Z/nZ) are used to count primes in residue classes.

name: Spectral ideas from vibrating systems and quadratic forms
summary: The eigenvalue idea first appeared in d'Alembert's treatment of a loaded string and Sturm's extension to differential systems, then Cauchy proved symmetric matrices diagonalise, joining quadratic forms with spectral theory.

name: D'Alembert and Euler: wave equation and PDEs
summary: The vibrating string led to the wave equation and series solutions.

name: Fundamental theorem of algebra: analytic and topological proofs
summary: d'Alembert and Argand proved existence of roots using minima of the modulus, while Gauss's first and third proofs are described as topological, importing non-algebraic methods into algebra.

name: Vibrating-string controversy and the general function concept
summary: The dispute between d'Alembert and Euler over admissible initial shapes pushed analysis from formulas toward arbitrary dependence, later made explicit in Euler's definition and Fourier's heat work.

name: Euler's Introductio
summary: Functions replaced curves as the object of calculus, with e^{ix} relation, exponentials and logs.
